report.summary: Chunk 2 of gated_writes.py: defines path rebasing, GatedCandidate dataclass, artifact root, relay gate, and recording runner.
risks: rebase_declared_path | medium | Process-spawn side effect via Path.resolve() which can trigger symlink resolution, but no actual spawn; effect is none. Settle by verifying no external process is invoked.
_artifact_root_for | medium | Uses LOCALAPPDATA or tempdir; writes to filesystem (base / 'daedalus' / 'artifacts' / ...). Settle by confirming directory creation is intended.

_relay_gate | high | Closure captures box dict; relies on external offload_runner and GateResult. Uncheckable correctness of gate logic without seeing offload_runner's behavior. Settle by reviewing offload_runner's return structure.
_recording_runner | high | Wraps offload_runner; assumes box is set before gate reads it. Uncheckable ordering guarantee without seeing TaskAttempt._run_with_ledger. Settle by auditing that file.
todos: Verify that offload_runner and GateResult exist in daedalus.spine.attempt and match expected interfaces.
Ensure _artifact_root_for creates the directory before writing (not shown in this chunk).
Consider adding type hints for GatedCandidate fields.

handoff.purpose: Defines path rebasing utilities, GatedCandidate dataclass, artifact storage root, relay gate function, and recording runner wrapper.

claims.text: An absolute path that resolves OUTSIDE ``primary_root`` is returned unchanged -- out of scope for rebasing, and left for downstream guards (offload's own path confinement) to refuse exactly as they do today.
claims.why: Code: if p.is_absolute() and try/except ValueError catches when resolve().relative_to fails, returns raw unchanged.

claims.text: ``spec`` is retained (not just ``result``) because ``AttemptResult`` does not carry the originating ``TaskSpec`` -- and Phase 2's staleness retry needs to re-attempt the SAME instruction/target_paths against a NEW ``base_revision``, which requires the original spec, not just its result.
claims.why: The claim references AttemptResult and TaskSpec from other modules; no code here verifies their interfaces.

claims.text: A held candidate cannot live only in ``AttemptResult.artifact``: ``run_write_wave`` returns plain dictionaries and ``TaskAttempt`` reaps its candidate branch, so those bytes otherwise disappear as soon as the call returns.
claims.why: References run_write_wave and TaskAttempt behavior not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Keep the archive beside the worktree/control state, namespaced by checkout identity, and let ``TaskAttempt._persist`` apply its primary-tree fence before it creates or writes anything.
claims.why: References TaskAttempt._persist and primary-tree fence not in this chunk.

claims.text: A gate callable only ever receives a ``RunnerContext`` (worktree/branch/base/task/is_cancelled) -- never the runner's return value -- so there is no direct way to ask "did offload() call this clean".
claims.why: RunnerContext interface not shown; claim about gate callable protocol not verifiable here.

claims.text: ``box`` is a mutable cell the paired runner (``_recording_runner``) writes its result into before returning; this closure reads it back.
claims.why: Code: _relay_gate receives box dict, reads box.get('result'); _recording_runner sets box['result'] before returning.

claims.text: Why not TaskAttempt's own default (``pytest_gate(task.gate_paths)``, a bare ``python -m pytest``)? It assumes pytest, which is not every project's test runner -- ``offload()``'s own ``verify()`` already runs the PROJECT'S configured ``test_command``, whatever that is. Running it again here would be a SECOND, independent verify of the same change, which is the "raw provider call" the standing orders say must not happen: offload's verify+rollback cascade is meant to stay the one authority for per-task correctness.
claims.why: References offload.verify, test_command, standing orders, and TaskAttempt default gate not present in this chunk.

claims.text: This still catches a real failure mode a bare "is the diff non-empty" check would miss: offload can finish with ``action == "escalated_after_verify_fail"`` while ``wrote`` is NON-EMPTY, because a write it could not fully roll back is reported in ``dirty_unreverted`` and kept in ``wrote`` so it stays visible. That leaves a non-empty artifact for a run offload itself considers FAILED, and only checking ``action == "offloaded"`` (not "artifact exists") refuses it.
claims.why: References offload's action values and wrote semantics not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: ``box["result"]`` is set the instant the runner returns, which is always BEFORE ``TaskAttempt`` calls the gate (see ``daedalus.spine.attempt.TaskAttempt._run_with_ledger``: runner, then artifact capture, then gate) -- so ``_relay_gate`` reading ``box`` always sees this attempt's own result, never a stale or missing one.
claims.why: References TaskAttempt._run_with_ledger and ordering not present; relies on external module.

observations.what: rebase_declared_path uses p.resolve() which may have side effects (symlink resolution) but no external process.
_artifact_root_for creates a path under LOCALAPPDATA or tempdir; no mkdir call in this chunk, so writing later may fail if directory absent.
GatedCandidate fields are typed as Any; no type enforcement.
_relay_gate returns a closure that captures box; it imports GateResult inside the closure, which is fine but unusual.
_recording_runner imports offload_runner inside the function, which is acceptable but may cause import overhead on each call.
